question.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{5x-22}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{5}{x-4}+\frac{B}{(x-4)^{2}},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
question.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-4)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-22 & =5(x-4)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=4$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5(4)-22 & =5(4-4)+B \\ -2 & =0+B \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
